sentences.sentence: NHS inform describes tension-type headache as the most common kind.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says tension headaches are not a sign of an underlying condition, and common triggers include stress, sleep problems and caffeine.
sentences.note: Summary: NHS says not a sign of an underlying condition; triggers stress, sleep problems, caffeine.

sentences.sentence: Migraine usually causes a moderate or severe throbbing pain, often on one side of the head.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Other migraine symptoms include feeling sick and sensitivity to light and sound.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Some people also get an aura, such as seeing zigzag lines or flashing lights.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says migraine affects around 1 in 5 women and 1 in 15 men.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Cluster headaches are rare, and each attack is intensely painful, affects one side of the head and can happen several times a day.
sentences.note: Summary of NHS inform cluster headache text.

sentences.sentence: Taking painkillers regularly can itself cause daily headaches, a problem called medication overuse headache.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says it usually affects people who already have tension-type headaches or migraines.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Stopping the overused medicine usually helps, although the pain can get worse for a few days first.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: People who get headaches often and take painkillers regularly are advised to speak to a GP.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E for a headache that comes on suddenly and is extremely painful, or one that follows a serious head injury.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Other reasons to call 999 include weakness on one side, slurred speech, trouble speaking or remembering, loss of vision, drowsiness, confusion, or a high temperature with a stiff neck or a rash that could mean meningitis.
sentences.note: Summary listed stroke-type signs, meningitis or sepsis signs, drowsiness, confusion, loss of vision.

sentences.sentence: NHS inform lists headaches that wake someone at night, that are there on waking, that keep getting worse, or that are set off by coughing, sneezing or bending as reasons for an urgent GP appointment or a call to NHS 111.
sentences.note: Summary [2-7]; page attribution to nhsinform headaches page uncertain.

sentences.sentence: A new headache in a person over 50, with a sore scalp or jaw pain when chewing, can signal inflamed arteries and also needs urgent attention.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Headaches with vision changes, or with vomiting plus dizziness or weakness, also call for urgent review.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: An NHS formulary guideline describes giant cell arteritis, also called temporal arteritis, as a medical emergency that needs prompt assessment and immediate steroid treatment to prevent permanent loss of vision.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: An NHS trust page lists tiredness, loss of appetite, weight loss, fever and headache, with tenderness over the temples, jaw or tongue pain when eating, and blurred vision, as its symptoms.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS pages describe triptans as a painkiller designed for migraine, which works by reversing the widening of blood vessels that is believed to be part of the migraine process.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: If ordinary painkillers do not relieve migraine symptoms, the NHS advises making a GP appointment.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Anti-sickness medicines can help during a migraine even without nausea, and the NHS says they work better when taken as soon as symptoms begin.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: An NHS-hosted leaflet advises against strong opioid painkillers such as codeine, tramadol and morphine for migraine because of the high risk of rebound headache.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS lists common migraine triggers as stress, tiredness, lack of sleep, dehydration, missing meals, regular alcohol or caffeine, and foods such as cheese or chocolate, and suggests keeping a record to spot personal triggers.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises seeing a GP for tension headaches that happen several times a week, are severe, or do not respond to painkillers and relaxation.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: These can be signs of a different type of headache, such as migraine or cluster headache.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A GP may suggest keeping a headache diary that records how often the headaches happen and how long they last.
sentences.note: Summary: NHS says a GP may suggest a headache diary.

sentences.sentence: There is no specific test for migraine, so the GP looks for a pattern of recurring headaches with the typical symptoms.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Simple painkillers, rest and fluids are the first step for most headaches.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: If painkillers and exercise do not help, a person may be referred to a specialist, and a medicine called amitriptyline may be offered to help prevent tension headaches.
